expected.title: A finite central skew field has a maximal separable subfield
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that a finite central skew field over a field contains a maximal subfield separable over the ground field, and hence that every Brauer class has a finite separable splitting field (statement lines 922-929). The proof is a complete argument: the class statement is reduced to the subfield statement by a named lemma, and the subfield statement is reduced to the existence of one separable element outside the ground field by passing to a centralizer (proof lines 931-953); assuming the contrary in positive characteristic, the author extracts a fixed p-power whose map sends the skew field into the ground field (proof lines 954-962), expresses that map in coordinates of a chosen basis and kills all coordinates above the first using the infinitude of the ground field (proof lines 964-972); extending scalars to the algebraic closure makes the algebra a matrix algebra in which a matrix unit has noncentral p-th power, giving the contradiction (proof lines 972-977). The non-formal content is the coordinate argument and the final matrix computation. The claim is H3.
